rows.name: Draw a square from the class's spoken instructions
steps: Educator stands at the board and draws a square only as the children's spoken instructions say.
If a child says 'Draw a line', draw a messy squiggle.
If a child says 'Turn', turn around in a circle.
Children see that clear distances and exact turns are needed and restate their instructions.
rows.materials: Board and marker (not named in the plan).

levels.0: Board shows only a squiggle: no instruction named a length or a turn.
levels.1: Instructions name lengths but skip a turn, so the board square has an open corner.
levels.2: Four equal sides and four turns are named in order, and the board square closes.
levels.3: Instructions are re-spoken shorter after a test, with a reason for each cut.

rows.name: Scratch: connect Green Flag to Move 50 Steps
steps: Open the full Scratch interface.

levels.1: Green Flag and Move 50 are on screen but not joined, until a block is nudged for the pupil.
levels.2: Clicking the flag moves the sprite 50 steps, and a changed count changes the distance.
levels.3: Written prediction for 80 steps matches the distance seen on the Stage.

rows.name: Human Keyboard
steps: When the educator claps once (input), the whole room shouts 'Beep!' (output).
When the educator stomps a foot (input), the whole room jumps up (output).
Children tell which action was the input and which the output.

levels.0: Room responds to claps and stomps in the wrong order or not at all.
levels.1: Right response to a clap but the stomp is missed until a neighbour moves.
levels.2: Beep follows every clap and a jump follows every stomp, and the pupil names clap as input and beep as output.
levels.3: Whistle-and-spin or another invented input and output pair is run with the class.

levels.1: Space plays the sound but the arrow block is missing its 10 steps.
levels.2: Space plays a sound and the right arrow shifts the sprite 10 steps along X.
levels.3: A third key block of the pupil's own is added and labelled input or output.

levels.2: Pages flipped fast make the stick figure wave, with fast pictures named as the cause.

rows.name: Number line from -5 to 20
steps: Lay a long strip of floor tape and mark 0.
Children write numbers on cards and place those below zero to the left.
Place cards from 0 to 20 to the right and read the line forwards and backwards.
Pick a start number and a rule such as +3; children walk and say the sequence.
Children order a jumbled set of number cards, including those below zero.

levels.0: Number cards are stacked unsorted beside the tape.
levels.1: Cards from 0 to 20 are in order but those below zero sit on the wrong side.
levels.2: Cards from -5 to 20 sit in order with zero marked, and the sequence is read forwards and backwards.
levels.3: Walking a fresh start number with a +3 rule, the sequence is called out.

rows.name: Place value to 10,000 with cards
steps: Give each pair digit cards and a place value mat (Th, H, T, O).
The educator calls out a number; the pair builds it on the mat.
Pairs read the number aloud and write it in digits.
Swap: one child builds, the other reads and writes.
Change one digit and read the new number.

levels.0: Mat is empty after the number is called.
levels.1: Digits go into columns but two are swapped.
levels.2: Called number is built, read aloud and written in digits correctly.
levels.3: Changing one digit produces a new number that is read right before the change is made.

Pairs find when a named lesson starts and show it on the clock.
Say am or pm for the time.
Given the start and the length of a lesson, find when it ends.
Find the gap between two lessons.

levels.0: Clock face shows no time for the lesson.
levels.1: Start time is shown but am or pm is left off.
levels.2: Start time is set on the clock face with am or pm, and the end time is found.
levels.3: Gap between two lessons is written in minutes.

levels.2: Three pairs of times give correct durations on the time line.
levels.3: A pair crossing noon is solved and checked backwards.
